question: According to the Indian Constitution, which of the following is the final authority in the interpretation of the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India is the **highest judicial authority** in the country and acts as the **final interpreter of the Constitution of India**.
 
• Under **Article 141** of the Indian Constitution, the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India, making it the ultimate authority in constitutional interpretation.
 
• The Supreme Court has the power of **judicial review** under **Article 13**, which allows it to declare any law or executive action unconstitutional if it violates the Constitution.
 
• In disputes involving the interpretation of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has the exclusive jurisdiction as per **Article 131**.
 
• It also acts as the guardian of the Constitution, ensuring that the principles and provisions of the Constitution are upheld by all branches of the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of the Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• The **Lok Sabha** is the lower house of the Parliament of India and represents the people of the country.
 
• It has the power to make laws and amend the Constitution, but the interpretation of the Constitution is not its function.
 
• Its actions are subject to judicial review by the Supreme Court to ensure compliance with the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President:**
 
 
• The **President of India** is the constitutional head of the executive branch, but they do not have the authority to interpret the Constitution.
 
• However, the President can seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion under **Article 143** on constitutional matters.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Parliament:**
 
 
• The Parliament has the authority to make and amend laws, including constitutional amendments.
 
• However, the constitutionality of laws enacted by the Parliament can be reviewed by the Supreme Court, which has the final say in interpretation.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• The power of **judicial review** enables the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders.
 
• It ensures that the laws passed by the legislature and actions taken by the executive comply with the Constitution.
 
• This power is a fundamental aspect of the **basic structure doctrine**, which cannot be altered even by constitutional amendments.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **Supreme Court** was established on **January 28, 1950**, under the Constitution of India.
 
• The Supreme Court comprises the Chief Justice of India and other judges, with the maximum strength fixed at **34 judges** (as per the 2019 amendment).
 
• The Supreme Court also has appellate jurisdiction, original jurisdiction, and advisory jurisdiction.
